name: Jaipongan
notes: Jaipongan style pack (Doc 04 template, solo-first). West Java's drum-cracked pride, and one of the clearest CREATED-TRADITION stories in world dance: JAIPONGAN was built by GUGUM GUMBIRA in 1970s Bandung — a Sundanese musician-choreographer who, in the era after Indonesia's leaders had pushed back against Western pop (Sukarno's early-60s campaign against 'ngak ngik ngok' rock), went deliberately INTO his own culture's roots: the village flirtation dance KETUK TILU, the martial coils of PENCAK SILAT, and the whipcrack accents of the KENDANG drum. The result, launched into the world through hits like 'Daun Pulus Keser Bojong', became Sunda's modern signature — and promptly generated the classic scandal: jaipongan's famous hip trio — GEOL (grind), GITEK (bump), GOYANG (sway) — drew moralist criticism and attempts to keep it off television in the early 1980s, and the dance won the way hip dances always win in this app's testimony: everyone was already dancing it. Gugum Gumbira died in 2020, mourned as a national treasure; his creation is taught openly in SANGGAR studios across West Java and by Sundanese teachers worldwide. Design truths: the kendang's language is the dance's language (the drummer marks the dancer — sabar's dialogue, Sundanese accent), the silat-derived poses give jaipongan its coiled architecture, and the 3G hip vocabulary is layered progressively. The kendang jaipong cycle rides in this app's Rhythm Trainer.

seasons.finale: Film yourself marking the kendang's cracks — every 'pak!' answered with a body accent, one full song.
Film the silat-derived stances and arm coils — low, wound, ready — held and flowed for one song.
Film the hip trio — geol, gitek, goyang — distinct, layered, and unapologetic.
Film a full jaipongan phrase: coiled entrance, hip vocabulary flowing, kendang cracks hit, held finish.
Learn eight counts from a Sundanese source video (sanggar or stage footage), credit it, and film your version beside it.

attributes.name: 3G hip control L2
attributes.test: 60s cycling geol-gitek-goyang on command — three distinct hip words, switchable mid-bar without blur

attributes.name: Coiled-stance legs L1
attributes.test: 90s in a low wound stance with soft knees and live weight shifts — silat's readiness without silat's contact

attributes.name: Crack-response ear L2
attributes.test: mark ten kendang accents in one song with sharp body hits, none late — the drummer is talking to you

nodes.name: The kendang — the drum that commands
checkpoints: jaipongan runs on the KENDANG — the two-headed Sundanese drum whose sharp 'pak!' cracks and rolling low strokes CONDUCT the dancer directly; the cycle is in this app's Rhythm Trainer
the drummer marks the dance: accents call hip hits, rolls call flows, stops call freezes — sabar's drum-dialogue principle with a Sundanese accent
learn the vocabulary by ear: the crack (sharp slap), the dut (deep boom), the roll — three sounds, three body responses

nodes.name: The gong cycle & the degung frame
checkpoints: under the kendang's chatter, the GONG marks the long cycle — the deep pulse that resets each phrase; feel the music breathe in gong-lengths, not bars
the Sundanese ensemble around it (saron, rebab, the sinden's voice) carries melody the hips answer
practice phrasing to the gong: build within the cycle, land your biggest accent just before the gong lands — riding the reset is jaipongan musicianship

nodes.name: Gugum Gumbira — the man who built it
checkpoints: JAIPONGAN WAS CREATED BY GUGUM GUMBIRA in 1970s Bandung — built deliberately from Sundanese roots: the village flirtation dance KETUK TILU, the martial coils of PENCAK SILAT, and the kendang's crack

the context matters: in the era after Indonesia's campaign against Western pop, he answered by going INTO his own culture, not around it — new tradition built proudly from local materials, launched through hits like 'Daun Pulus Keser Bojong'
he died in 2020, mourned as a national treasure — a named, dated, documented creator of a 'traditional' dance: kpanlogo's lesson, Sundanese chapter

nodes.name: The 3G scandal — the ban that failed, again
checkpoints: jaipongan's hip trio — GEOL, GITEK, GOYANG — drew moralist criticism and early-1980s attempts to keep it off Indonesian television for indecency
the ban failed the way this app has now documented five times: everyone was already dancing it — ndombolo, kpanlogo, the waltz, and jaipongan share the same biography
today it is Sunda's modern signature, taught in sanggar studios and school stages — yesterday's scandal, today's heritage, the usual schedule

nodes.name: The coiled stance — silat's gift
checkpoints: the base: low, wound, asymmetric stances borrowed from pencak silat — knees soft, weight coiled onto one side, arms carving guarded curves
the coil is potential energy: every jaipongan pose looks one heartbeat from springing — stillness with a fuse in it
flow stance to stance on the kendang's rolls, freeze on the cracks — the drum decides when the coil winds and when it strikes
mistakes: standing tall and square (jaipongan's architecture is wound and angled — height releases the spring early)

nodes.name: The 3G trio — geol, gitek, goyang
nodes.anchor: the vocabulary they tried to ban
checkpoints: three distinct hip words: GEOL — the slow grinding circle; GITEK — the sharp sideways bump; GOYANG — the continuous easy sway; drill them as separate vocabulary before mixing
the kendang assigns them: rolls get goyang's flow, cracks get gitek's hit, the low dut gets geol's grind — the drum conjugates your hips
unapologetic is the register: this is the vocabulary that survived a TV ban — dance it with exactly that much confidence
mistakes: blurring the three into one wiggle (three words — a viewer should be able to name which you said)

nodes.name: Arm coils, fans & the selendang line
checkpoints: the arms carve silat's guarded curves made ornamental — wrapping coils, sudden extensions, wrists flicking like the kendang cracks made visible
the selendang (shoulder scarf) is the classic prop: flicked, wrapped, and trailed as an extension of the arm's line — any long scarf trains it
arms and hips converse: an arm extension answers a gitek, a wrap answers a geol — the body agreeing with itself loudly

nodes.name: Hitting the cracks
checkpoints: the signature skill: the kendang's 'pak!' lands and the whole body HITS with it — a gitek, a head snap, a freeze — zero latency, total commitment
train with real recordings: mark every crack in one song with a clap first, then with the body — the ear leads the hips by a week
between cracks, melt: the contrast between the flowing goyang and the knife-sharp hit is jaipongan's whole electricity
mistakes: hitting late (a late crack-hit reads as a stumble — if the ear isn't ready, go back to clapping)

nodes.name: The full phrase — coil, flow, crack, finish
checkpoints: assemble the sentence: coiled entrance, goyang carrying travel, geol grinding the low section, gitek and arm-flicks hitting cracks, a wound finish landing just before the gong
phrase in gong-lengths: one complete idea per cycle, bigger each cycle — the build discipline every style in this app shares
borrow one phrase from sanggar or stage footage, credited in your journal — learning from Sundanese sources is the pack's standing order

nodes.name: The Bandung set — filmed
checkpoints: film one full song: stance coiled, 3G distinct, arms conversing, every audible crack hit, phrases landing on the gong
the vocabulary audit: pause on three hip moments and name them — if you can't tell your geol from your goyang, neither can the kendang
say it on camera: jaipongan, created by Gugum Gumbira, Bandung, from ketuk tilu and silat — the creator's name is the first credit, every time

nodes.name: The sanggar door
checkpoints: find it live: sanggar studios across West Java teach openly, Indonesian cultural nights and embassies run workshops worldwide, and Sundanese teachers post real instruction online
at an Indonesian festival, jaipongan is the floor-filler — join with the goyang and let the kendang upgrade you
tell one person the Gugum Gumbira story — a dance with a birth certificate is the best argument this app owns against 'anonymous folk culture'
